title: v1/chat: param coercion, deterministic stop semantics, and stream sentinel reconciliation
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Normalize v1/chat param types (coercion for legacy callers); make stop-array handling deterministic and documented; improve stream sentinel reconciliation to avoid duplicate tokens at fragment boundaries.
description:
Context: Customers expect Redwood's /v1/chat compatibility layer to behave like OpenAI's chat completions for a wide range of legacy callers. We observed two classes of subtle but production-impacting differences: (1) callers passing loosely-typed params (e.g. "max_tokens" as string or stop as single string vs array) which produced surprising errors or different internal routing; (2) streaming edge cases where a sentinel (final fragment) and the last delta caused duplicated partial tokens or an out-of-order logprob envelope. This PR introduces a small compatibility shim that coercively normalizes incoming v1 chat params, clarifies/standardizes stop-array semantics, and strengthens the stream sentinel reconciliation handshake so that the final token is emitted exactly once and structured envelopes are preserved.

What this changes (summary): 1) Param coercion layer under server/proxy/openai_compat/param_coercer.py that safely coerces strings to numbers, coerces single stop string -> [string], and normalizes role aliases (assistant/system/user -> expected tokens). Coercion only runs on v1/chat entrypoints and is opt-out via a config flag. 2) Deterministic stop handling: stop arrays are canonicalized (de-duplicated, ordered by earliest-match precedence) and a clear tie-breaker is applied for overlapping stop sequences. This addresses customer reports where stop arrays produced non-deterministic truncation. 3) Stream sentinel reconciliation: added a lightweight handshake between the stream coordinator and the fragment assembler that tags sentinel fragments and defers final flush until the handshake confirms no trailing delta will arrive. The result eliminates a class of duplicate-character artifacts and prevents mis-merged logprob envelopes when function/tool-call fragments cross chunk boundaries.

Why this approach: Full strict validation broke many existing users that relied on forgiving behavior. A coercion shim provides a smoother migration path and reduces customer friction while keeping runtime invariant checks. The stream reconciliation is intentionally conservative (small delay window + deterministic ordering) to preserve latency SLOs while fixing correctness.

Checklist: - [x] Param coercion implementation + unit tests - [x] Stop-array canonicalization + unit tests - [x] Stream sentinel reconciliation + integration test (simulated chunk races) - [x] End-to-end QA against openai-compat test vectors - [x] Feature flag added and documented - [x] Back-compat smoke tests against production traffic sample

Testing notes: Added ~30 unit tests and 3 integration scenarios that replay previously failing traces (included as fixtures in tests/fixtures/stream-replay). Verified redis-backed KV-cache behaviour unchanged. Load-tested the stream coordinator under small variance and measured median latency increase of <0.5ms (within noise) with the reconciliation active.

Related: ENG-3412 (param stability), SUP-712 (customer incident #1223), ENG-3499 (streaming flake investigations).

Merge: squash and merge after CI green and one approval.

qa_notes: Replay of production failing trace #1223 demonstrates stop array overlap previously truncating on the wrong boundary; after this change the output matches OpenAI v1 reference vectors. No user-visible change unless caller relied on previous nondeterminism. The coercion flag is off by default and will be enabled for the next minor release after staged rollout.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: coercion layer is reversible and feature-flagged; any customer needing strict validation should enable strict-mode via config. Observability hooks added to track how many requests are coerced for 30d telemetry.
